facts.text: Eldoret was founded in 1910 when Willie van Aardt received block No. 1910, marking the town’s official start.
The town earned the nickname Farm 64 after settlers numbered their plots, a quirky legacy still remembered by locals.
Eldoret hosts Kenya’s first small‑arms manufacturer, the Kenya Ordnance Factories Corporation, which began production in 1997.
Toyota Tsusho built Kenya’s first full‑scale fertilizer blending plant at Ngeria, just outside Eldoret, boosting regional agriculture.
Athletes worldwide flock to Eldoret’s high‑altitude training centers, where the IAAF’s facility and local camps help shape Olympic champions.
Daima Towers, standing 70 metres tall, is the tallest building west of Nairobi and a landmark of Eldoret’s skyline.
